newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Lung Kee Metals sees 20 pct growth.
newsitem.headline: Lung Kee Metals sees 20 pct growth.

text.p: Lung Kee Metal Holdings, part of Hong Kong's Lung Kee has targetted a 20 percent growth in turnover a year, said executive director William Wai on Monday.
"It is our internal strategy to grow (turnover) by 20 percent every year," Wai told a news conference.
For the financial year ended March 1997, the mould base maker's turnover was HK$396.08 million, while net profit was HK$98.46 million.
"It is our strategy to continue to produce in low-cost areas like China and Malaysia but target markets worldwide like Hong Kong, China, Malaysia, Japan and Europe," Wai said.
He said the group was studying opportunities of setting up more plants in the region.
"For the next five years, we may build more plants," he said, citing examples in northern and western China as well as India, he said.
In India, the group planned to start marketing its products through an agent to test the field before entering deeper through a joint venture with a local company or on its own.
He gave an estimated investment budget of HK$30-40 million to set up one new plant.
"Every year, we have budgeted HK$60-70 million to replace old machines, add new ones and for setting up new plants," Wai said.
The group now has most of its production sites in China and Malaysia.
